question.problem:
The matrix $C$ and the vector $b$ are given below.
Determine if $b\in \text{Col}(C).$ 
In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}$, where ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are real numbers such that $b={x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}+{x}_{3}{c}_{3},$ and ${c}_{1}$, ${c}_{2}$, and ${c}_{3}$ are the respective columns of $C.$

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -4 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -8 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(C),$ we need to check if the equation $Cx=b$ is consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[C\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[C\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -4 & 9 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & -8 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & ↔{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 5 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & -8 \\ 4 & 1 & -4 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -3 \\ 4 & 1 & -4 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -3 \\ 0 & -7 & -16 & -11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(\frac{7}{3}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -9 & -18\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=5 \\ 3{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-3 \\ -9{x}_{3}=-18.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=2.$ Substituting it into the second equation gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{2}+3(2) & =-3 \\ {x}_{2} & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, from the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =5-2{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} \\  & =5-2(-3)-3(2) \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Since we have a solution, the equation $Cx=b$ is consistent, which implies that $b\in \text{Col}(C).$ 

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${c}_{1},$ ${c}_{2},$ and ${c}_{3}:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -8 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}=5\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{c}_{1}}+(-3)\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{c}_{2}}+2\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{c}_{3}}
$$

Finally, we get ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}=5\cdot (-3)\cdot 2=-30.$
